It's very pleasant to take a shower and watch the city wake up. To see how the orange rays of the sun start creating shadows on the tall buildings.

Sometimes I open the window a bit to get a better view, and even though I risk some water spilling into the laundry patio, it's worth the spectacle. I also like the intense cold burst that comes from opening the window a little in the middle of the shower.
It revitalizes, wakes me up, the contrast feels good.

Lately, as I come out, an impatient little animal waits for me, sitting on its small hind legs, waiting for me to step onto the bath mat, so it can refresh itself with my wet ankles and shins. It rubs against me and purrs, gets its fur wet, and meows contentedly. Soon, it starts to nibble and scratch, and with bare feet, that's something you don't want to happen.

At that moment, it becomes urgent to put on shoes to avoid its tiny teeth, sharp as blades, but it's more important to build bonds with the little life form in the house. In the end, that's what makes the four walls our home: the little nibbles on the ankles.

So the urgent will have to wait.

I don't like focusing on the urgent because its measure is time, and time is very relative. That's why we find ourselves in situations where what was urgent today is no longer urgent tomorrow. We have to constantly deal with these occasions.

On the other hand, the measure of importance is consequences, and that I like more. I like doing things thinking about the "why" and not so much the "what," even discarding seemingly serious tasks simply because I wasn't doing them for the right reason. There have also been instances where I find myself doing seemingly insignificant things but where the reason was the most important. Again, the "why" before the "what."

What's important, unlike what's urgent, rarely stops being important. That's why I prefer to focus on what's important.

Because priorities change, because the future is uncertain, because we humans are terrible at predicting what will happen or understanding what we really want.

Despite everything, what's important will remain important. At most, we can ignore it, as if we could escape, but reality won't change.

Normally, this has worked for me, and for now, I have no complaints. Well, one complains when their bare feet get bitten after a shower, but it's always worth choosing the important over the urgent.
